title: Go SDK streaming connection lifecycle, deadline-aware reads, and retry semantics
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers using the Go SDK's streaming API need predictable, idiomatic behavior when callers cancel contexts or when deadlines elapse mid-stream. Current behavior is inconsistent: some streams return io.EOF, some return wrapped transport errors, and some goroutines leak when a context is cancelled during a read. This ticket designs and implements a consistent lifecycle model: clear semantics for cancellation vs. deadline expiration, backpressure-friendly chunk delivery, and documented retry boundaries for streams.

Goals:
- Define and implement a stream session type that respects ctx cancellation and deadlines consistently across transport layers.
- Ensure no goroutine leaks on client-side cancellation or server-initiated stream termination.
- Provide a clear retry policy for resumable vs non-resumable streams and surface a small ergonomic API for common use cases.
- Add unit/integration tests and an examples page showing idiomatic usage (timeout per-response, graceful shutdown).
acceptance_criteria: Go SDK exposes a StreamSession type with Read/Recv and Close methods; operations respect ctx cancellation and deadlines and return context.Canceled or context.DeadlineExceeded where appropriate
Canceling the passed context causes active reads to return promptly and cleans up internal goroutines within 50ms in tests
Examples in docs show two patterns: (a) single ctx for whole call (deadline for entire run), (b) per-chunk short deadlines for low-latency UIs
Retry behavior documented: client automatically retries idempotent prelude/handshake only; streaming deltas are not retried by default, with an opt-in resume token API
Integration test against local test server simulating mid-stream network flaps passes in CI
PR is linked, reviewed by Runtime and SDK leads, and approved
design_notes: Introduce StreamSession interface: Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error) and Close() error. Avoid exposing io.Reader directly to surface context-aware Recv API.
Use a buffered internal channel for chunks to decouple transport read goroutine from consumer backpressure. Channel size default 8 with opt-in config.
On ctx cancellation: close the transport, cancel internal goroutines, then return context.Canceled from in-flight Recv calls. For deadline expiry return context.DeadlineExceeded.
For transports that already return HTTP/2/gRPC errors, map common codes to context errors when ctx is done to avoid confusing wrapped errors.

Retry model: only retry pre-stream setup (auth, model resolution). Streaming payloads are considered non-idempotent unless the server supplies a resume token. If resume token present, expose Resume(ctx, token) API and document semantics.
Expose high-level helper: StreamWithTimeout(ctx, client, opts, perChunkTimeout) that wraps Recv to create short per-chunk contexts while preserving overall ctx for cancellation
Add metrics: stream.active, stream.recv_latency_ms, stream.cancelled_by_client to Console traces for debugging customer incidents
implementation_plan: 1) Spec PR: add StreamSession interface and examples to SDK README (small standalone RFC).
2) Implement transport adapters (http/1.1 chunked, http/2, grpc) to produce unified chunk envelopes and resume tokens.
3) Implement goroutine lifetime management: one transport reader -> send to buffered channel -> consumer Recv drains channel. Close path drains and clears resources.
4) Add mapping layer to convert transport errors into context errors when ctx is done (with unit tests for each mapping).
5) Add helper functions and example code for per-chunk deadlines and graceful shutdown patterns.
6) Write integration tests with a flaky test server simulating delays and cancels; run against CI and a dedicated heavy-load test to check for leaks.
7) Docs: add new page under SDK "Streaming patterns" and a short migration guide from older Stream API.
8) Code review, merge, and ship in go-sdk-1.6 with a short blog note about improved streaming ergonomics.
